claims.text: Adding 2–3 at.% hafnium to the refractory high-entropy alloy will improve its radiation tolerance.
Adding 2–3 at.% hafnium will not compromise the alloy's mechanical integrity under plasma-facing conditions.
The baseline is a hafnium-free refractory high-entropy alloy based on elements such as Mo, Nb, Ta, and W.
The beneficial effect should occur during high-flux irradiation at approximately 600–900°C using irradiation representative of fusion-reactor conditions.
Hafnium has a larger atomic size and different bonding characteristics than the principal elements of the baseline alloy.
Hafnium addition will locally distort the alloy lattice.
Hafnium addition will facilitate formation of hafnium-rich nanoclusters or segregated regions.
Hafnium-rich nanoclusters or segregated regions will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The proposed defect sinks will promote annihilation or recombination of radiation-induced interstitials and vacancies.
Enhanced point-defect recombination will suppress coalescence of point defects into larger mechanically deleterious clusters.
Suppressing defect coalescence will preserve mechanical strength after irradiation.
The hafnium-modified alloy will have at least approximately 20% lower radiation-induced defect density than the unmodified baseline.
The hafnium-modified alloy will maintain, or only minimally change, hardness and tensile strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
Under comparable irradiation, the hafnium-free baseline will accumulate more radiation-induced defects and undergo noticeable mechanical degradation.
The predicted benefit is contingent on achieving a uniform distribution of hafnium in the alloy.
Processing-route changes or large deviations from the specified irradiation environment may alter the hafnium effect.

contradictions.description: The mediator requires hafnium-rich nanoclusters or segregated regions, whereas the boundary condition requires a uniform hafnium distribution. These can coexist only if 'uniform' refers to macroscopic homogeneity with controlled nanoscale clustering, but that distinction is not stated.
